_comment: EXAMPLE ONLY - this is a shape reference, not content. What the arenas of a run actually look
like is DELIBERATELY NOT DECIDED (plan §2.29 fixed the mechanism and left the blocks open), so
Unlike the biome example there is no 'weight' to disable: a palette does nothing until something
names it. Nothing ships naming this one, so it is inert. Copy it, rename it, change the blocks.
One palette per file. The id is the file path: this one is 'cobblemon_roguelite:example', and a
file at .../arena_palettes/volcano/summit.json in namespace 'ns' would be 'ns:volcano/summit'.
Any field whose name starts with '_' is ignored, which is where comments go. Every other
unknown field is an error, so a typo is reported instead of silently taking a default.
The atmosphere is NOT built here. Sky colour, fog, water and grass tint, ambient loops and music
all come from the biome file's 'minecraft_biome' repaint (§2.24). This is only the floor you
stand on, in the right colour. A basalt platform under orange fog reads as a volcano; the same
platform under a snowy biome reads as a caldera. That is the intended division of labour.
_floor: The platform, one block layer, at the very bottom of the arena box - which is where the player
is put down. Required, and it may not be 'minecraft:air': an arena of air is a run with no floor
in a void dimension. Any registered block id, from any mod; an id nothing provides refuses the
arena by name rather than quietly placing nothing.
Blocks are placed in their DEFAULT state, so naming a stair or a slab gets you the default
facing. Use the arena_template override on a biome if you need real block states.
_width_depth: Platform size in blocks, centred in the arena box. Both optional - omit them and the platform
fills the box footprint (64x64 by default). Minimum 3x3. Larger than the box is refused, with
both numbers in the message, because everything that tidies an arena up works on the box.
_rim: An optional wall one block thick around the platform edge, standing on the floor. Not decoration:
the dimension is void and the platform has an edge, so this is the difference between a player
who walks off and a player who does not. Omit the whole object for no rim; 'height' defaults to 1.
_pillars: Four optional columns at the platform corners, standing on the floor. The only purely-decorative
field here, and cheap - four columns is a few dozen blocks. 'inset' is how far in from the corner
each one sits; 0 puts them in the rim, which is legal and means the pillar wins those cells.
_power_spot: Whether to place Mega Showdown's power_spot, one block off the platform centre (§2.5). TRUE is
the default and should stay true: the entire Tera/Dynamax confinement is 'this block exists
inside an arena and nowhere else', so setting it false is a biome where those gimmicks silently
do not work. It exists as a field so an owner who has banned them can say so.
Mega Showdown is a soft dependency. On a server without it the block is missing, that is logged
as an error naming the id, and the arena is built anyway - a Dynamax-less arena is playable.
